body.estimand_functional: \(\mathcal R(C)=\{D\in\mathfrak S_p:\mathsf S(D)=\mathsf S(C)\}\), certified on inequality by \(\mathsf{Route}(C,D)\)

sampling_model.design: The identification kernel compares full positive-definite covariance images of centred linear Gaussian SEMs; the statistical rung uses independent Gaussian sampling and global BIC over the finite labelled state class.
sampling_model.units: Each observation is one independent realization of the \(p\)-variable system with known zero mean.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment in the structure-identification kernel; ordered pairs in \(\mathcal Q\) index downstream interventions and responses.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; every innovation variance is positive and otherwise unrestricted.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Target-local block-incidence regressions estimate one coefficient per parent block and one residual variance per target. The effect maps use the same constrained regressions before finite path summation. The inferential claims are fixed in \(p\), pointwise outside \(\mathcal E_C\), and conditional on global rather than greedy optimization.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 19 proves structural identifiability within BPEC-DAGs, whose edge-colour classes all have size at least two, and Question 20 asks for a graphical characterization of edge-coloured model equivalence.
Theorem 2 transforms equivalent DAGs through exactly their distinct disagreeing edges, each reversed while covered.
Theorem 2.17 characterizes generic covariance-submatrix rank by trek separation and determinant expansions.
The paper explains classes of nested covariance constraints through restricted trek separation but gives no uniform arithmetic-height witness for coefficient-coloured model inequivalence.
Theorem 4.1 characterizes partial-homoscedastic model equivalence by ordinary Markov equivalence and fixed parent sets for vertices in nonsingleton variance blocks.
Theorem 4.4 characterizes existence and uniqueness of the MLE in a fixed compatibly coloured RDAG by linear independence of augmented sample vectors.
The paper gives linear-delay enumeration of ordinary Markov-equivalent DAGs and consistent extensions under background knowledge.
The paper extends Schwarz-type model-selection asymptotics to a finite collection of smoothly curved submodels of an exponential family.
The paper derives asymptotic inference for graph-indexed joint-intervention effects over an ordinary estimated Markov-equivalence class.
The paper constructs test-inversion confidence regions for total effects under equal error variances while accounting for structural uncertainty.

body.tldr: Target-local equality constraints among structural coefficients encode causal communities, but permitting singleton communities restores observational ambiguity. The headline result is a constructive necessity theorem: every mismatch of the proposed static signature is exposed by a unit-noise covariance generated from at most two coefficient-one blocks at one target, with integer entries bounded by \(p\) and an exact determinant or cleared-regression value in \(\{-2,-1,1,2\}\). This bounded separator yields covariance-model equality if and only if static-signature equality if and only if connectivity by legal singleton covered reversals, together with exact component enumeration. A qualified fixed-\(p\) rung then targets generic global-BIC recovery of the component and simultaneous pointwise inference for its member-labelled total-effect set.

project_justification.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 proves identifiability only when every blocked edge-colour class is nonsingleton and leaves graphical equivalence open. Its rational constraints and the determinant machinery of SullivantTalaskaDraisma2010 and DrtonRobevaWeihs2020 do not provide a uniformly small observable witness when singleton blocks are admitted.
project_justification.niche: The target-local blocked class has enough structure for every skeleton, collider, block-family, or unequal-family orientation mismatch to be routed to one sparse star calculation, while still containing ordinary Markov equivalence and the proper BPEC boundary as opposite special cases.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the four-case binary-star router and logarithmic numerical-height guarantee, lifts Chickering's disagreement-decreasing sequence to the exact legal blocked move graph, enumerates the resulting component, and attaches pointwise generic selection and effect-set inference without claiming uniformity at model intersections.

body.related_work: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 provides the writing and model exemplar: its Introduction moves from equality-constrained causal coefficients to causal communities, Theorem 19 proves proper BPEC identifiability, and Question 20 isolates general edge-coloured equivalence; the present strict advance is confined to target-local blocked colours with singleton blocks and adds bounded constructive separators. Chickering1995, Theorems 1 and 2, supplies the ordinary skeleton-collider criterion and the disagreement-decreasing covered-reversal induction; the new step is proving that equal blocked signatures force every selected move to be singleton and partition-compatible. SullivantTalaskaDraisma2010 supplies the determinant-expansion viewpoint, while DrtonRobevaWeihs2020 supplies the cleared rational-constraint analogue; both inform the certificate proof but are not claimed to be sharpened in their general graph classes. WuDrton2023 gives the nearest complete partition-restricted equivalence theorem for innovation variances, a different parameter restriction. MakamReichenbachSeigal2023 supplies the target-local pooled-regression likelihood construction. WienobstLuttermannBannachLiskiewicz2023 informs consistent-extension enumeration with background arrows. Haughton1988 informs the smooth finite-model BIC argument. NandyMaathuisRichardson2017 and StriederDrton2023 inform the simultaneous effect-set inference rung. Targeted searches through September 2026 found no paper occupying the bounded binary-star target-method pair or the stated singleton-permitting blocked equivalence criterion.
body.technical_internal_limitation: An independent exact-arithmetic implementation generated \(1\), \(3\), \(34\), \(1621\), and \(348631\) blocked states for \(p=1,2,3,4,5\). It verified every one of the \(1310886\) unequal-signature pairs at \(p=4\), including \(156\) unequal-family reversed-edge pairs, and all \(93380\) such reversed-family pairs at \(p=5\), using exact determinant or cleared-regression evaluation. These finite checks support but do not prove the all-\(p\) router. The statistical rung still requires full proofs of smooth embeddedness, properness of every exceptional locus, likelihood localization, and variance consistency.
body.honest_scope: Population equivalence allows zero coefficients and all positive innovation variances and makes no faithfulness assumption. The bounded separator and complete equivalence claims remain to be proved for all \(p\). The enumeration claim is finite and exact; no unverified linear-delay refinement is promised. Statistical conclusions are global-optimizer, fixed-\(p\), pointwise, and generic. Greedy GECS consistency, growing dimension, uniform inference near model intersections, cross-target edge-colour classes, constrained innovation variances, and cyclic graphs are outside scope.
